dedupe_keys.name: street level sendai framework implementation in greek civil protection census surveys of gscp and fire service staff 2025

description: These two survey data sets record how staff of Greece's civil protection agencies say the international Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction is actually put into practice in their day-to-day work. The producer is Theodora Blioumi of the University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice, who surveyed every eligible employee of the General Secretariat for Civil Protection, the ministry responsible for civil protection and disaster risk management, and in the larger survey also officials of the Fire Service. Coverage is national Greece, collected online between 27 October and 6 November 2025, with 74 valid responses in the first file and 130 in the second. Items on a one-to-five scale cover the framework's four priorities, understanding risk, governance, investment in resilience and preparedness for response and recovery, along with whether respondents served on the mainland or islands and their role; the second file underpins a Street-Level Sendai Implementation Index. The files are available as free downloads from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: self-reported perceptions from voluntary responses, and item wording is in the documentation. Simulation uses: parameters for the institutional capacity of emergency services in resilience models, and comparing preparedness across island and mainland services. Related records: the Ireland fire service statistics (data-ireland-fire-service-statistics-2016) describe another national emergency service.
name: Street-level Sendai Framework implementation in Greek civil protection: census surveys of GSCP and Fire Service staff (2025)
